purpose: Product/usability readiness for a non-scored human dry run -- NOT a research validation sample.

B_module_id_404_noise.current_finding: STILL REPRODUCIBLE -- the Architectural Explanation button/panel were shown and auto-fetched for ANY selected node, including non-symbol module/package/component-group container ids that api/routes/architectural_explanation.py always 404s for

Click Save to apply these settings.' Any unsaved edit shows a persistent 'Configuration has unsaved changes' hint until Save is clicked.
settings_usability.live_verification: baseline (clean, already-saved) state screenshot captured (02-settings-current-state.png); the dirty-state hint itself verified via the 2 new component tests rather than an additional live capture

dry_run_session_policy.launcher: start-lauras.ps1 / stop-lauras.ps1 (Vite dev server for the frontend + uvicorn dev server for the backend) -- this IS the actual accepted launcher; Laura's is NOT a packaged desktop application, and this is stated honestly in docs/usability-dry-run/README.md

dry_run_repository.rationale: public, already validated, relatively strong deterministic coverage, multiple navigable entities/supported claims known, reduces risk the session becomes a static-analysis-limitation exercise rather than a usability one

readiness_walkthrough.method: real browser (Playwright + real Chromium) driving the actual UI end to end, no internal API substitution for navigation

steps_verified.legacy_provider_traffic: not applicable to this round -- no legacy investigation-provider calls occurred; only architectural-explanation OpenAI requests were made

unplanned_finding_during_walkthrough.description: A real, transient ssl.SSLError ('bad record mac', a corrupted/dropped TLS record mid-response -- a genuine network condition, not a code defect) occurred on the first Architectural Explanation request. It surfaced as a raw, unhandled HTTP 500 with no Retry/Settings guidance, instead of the friendly 'Architectural explanation unavailable' UX every other network-failure class already gets.
unplanned_finding_during_walkthrough.root_cause: OpenAICompatibleInvestigationModel.complete_json only wrapped urllib.error.HTTPError/URLError into RuntimeError (which _verify_claims_or_503 catches and converts to a friendly 503); a bare ssl.SSLError is not a URLError subclass and escaped unwrapped.
unplanned_finding_during_walkthrough.fix: Also catch OSError (ssl.SSLError's base class) and wrap it the same way.
unplanned_finding_during_walkthrough.live_recapture_after_fix: not performed -- the exact transient condition is not reliably reproducible on demand, and the backend restart required to load the fix cleared the runtime-only OpenAI credential (expected, documented behavior -- see docs/OPENAI_CONFIGURATION.md 'Credential handling'). The fix is verified via 2 new, deterministic unit tests instead. Re-entering the credential and re-confirming success is now the first step of docs/usability-dry-run/SESSION_CHECKLIST.md, before any actual participant session.
unplanned_finding_during_walkthrough.second_entity_in_same_run_succeeded: the wsgi_app entity's explanation request (same run, same backend, before the fix) returned HTTP 200 -- confirming the failure was a one-off transient condition, not a systemic outage

backend_dev_reload_incident.description: Editing llm_model.py while the dev backend was live triggered uvicorn's --reload watcher mid-request; the backend process did not come back up cleanly and had to be restarted via stop-lauras.ps1 + start-lauras.ps1. This is a consequence of live-editing product code during this readiness round, not a defect exposed by or relevant to an actual dry-run participant (a participant's session does not edit product source).
backend_dev_reload_incident.resulting_credential_loss: expected/documented -- see docs/OPENAI_CONFIGURATION.md 'Credential handling'; addressed via SESSION_CHECKLIST.md step 4

product_commits_this_round.summary: Distinguish a successful connection test from a saved/enabled configuration
Auto-collapse the accessible-table overlay on a background click
Gate Architectural Explanation to symbol entities only
Wrap low-level socket/TLS errors as friendly RuntimeError, not raw 500

final_state.openai_credential_note: cleared by the dev-reload/restart incident above; must be re-entered via Settings before an actual participant session (SESSION_CHECKLIST.md step 4) -- this is normal, documented, process-memory-only credential behavior, not a defect

verdict: READY FOR NON-SCORED HUMAN DRY RUN
verdict_rationale: All explicitly re-audited items resolved with bounded, tested fixes (accessible-table auto-collapse; module-id 404 gating; Settings dirty-state clarity; friendly-error wrapping for low-level network failures). Startup/operator docs verified against current running behavior and one stale doc (OPENAI_CONFIGURATION.md) corrected. Full real-browser walkthrough completed end to end on the chosen dry-run repository (Flask, pinned commit) with zero developer shortcuts. The one live blocker discovered (raw 500 on a transient network error) was found, root-caused, fixed, and verified via targeted unit tests plus the full backend suite -- not deferred. The only outstanding action before a real session is re-entering the OpenAI API key in Settings, which is a normal, already-documented pre-session step now codified as SESSION_CHECKLIST.md's first action, not a product blocker.
